newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: France sees EU summit set for pact deal - official.
newsitem.headline: France sees EU summit set for pact deal - official.

text.p: A senior French official said on Sunday that France's leaders all wanted an agreement on a growth-and-jobs resolution enabling them to conclude an EMU stability pact at this week's Amsterdam summit.
The official said after President Jacques Chirac and new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin met on Saturday night to coordinate a single French position:
"The possibilities for an agreement exist... we all want to conclude," the official told reporters.

The official said there had been progress in the last few days both on an employment chapter in the revised Maastricht treaty on European union and on a separate resolution on measures to coordinate EU economic policies to promote growth and jobs.
"We want not only to consolidate what already exists or is on the table in the draft treaty but we also want to go further.
"Things have moved forward in the last few days and we think there is a possibility to go further," the official said.

Asked whether Jospin agreed with Chirac on the need to reach a deal in Amsterdam by Tuesday, the official replied: "There is a single French position in all areas. There are no differences between the president and Mr Jospin... We all want to conclude."

The official said the Dutch presidency had provided for finance ministers to hold a separate formal meeting on Monday, reporting their conclusions to the summit leaders at 5 PM (1500 GMT). The leaders would then discuss for the first time the issues of the stability pact and a resolution on jobs, growth and coordinating economic policies.
